indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters turn up in an unexpected order, so these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a stretch of Kent turns out to be unexpectedly dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' shuffles all thirteen letters of GOSH, KENT and AREAS into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something unremarkable or mediocre, which is what ordinary means here.

clue.text: Upset, being given piece of advice

definitions.meaning: to upset a cup is to knock it over, overturn it
someone given a useful hint or tip-off has been ...

explanation.surface: A person is distressed after receiving some unwelcome counsel.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the verb: knocked over, and given a hint, as in tipped for promotion.

parts.note: something unfashionable is out, no longer in vogue
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A clique that is no longer trendy is introduced, as an opening example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a start' reads as a phrase meaning 'to begin with'; here only 'start' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The outset of something is its very beginning, a synonym for its start.

clue.text: No end of danger for fairy-like creature

indicators.note: no end of tells us the last letter of the word for danger is dropped

parts.note: peril is danger

explanation.surface: Suggests endless risk facing some sprite of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like 'lots of', but it removes the final L from PERIL.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian mythology a peri is a beautiful spirit or elf, hence a fairy-like being.

parts.note: 'Well!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'Wow!'

indicators.note: sounds says that the word for a left-winger is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist, a left-winger

explanation.surface: Someone is impressed that a socialist comes across as clever.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has read widely is learned, so the phrase is a synonym for knowledgeable.

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the word art

explanation.surface: Praises the skilful person running a school or college art department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' looks like a job title, but it takes only the A of 'art'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adjectives for being highly skilled at something, so they are synonyms.

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of the word right are put into an incorrect order

explanation.surface: Someone checks a waist size and is told it is incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' reads as the reply to 'right?', but it is the signal to rearrange RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Girth is the distance around something, such as a person's middle.

indicators.note: hiding among says the letter for son sits concealed inside the word for trees

parts.note: a thicket is a dense cluster of trees or shrubs

explanation.surface: A well-built boy conceals himself in a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A thickset person is heavily built and solid, a synonym for sturdy.

clue.text: To leader of Greeks, a Roman habit

indicators.note: leader of picks out the initial letter of Greeks

explanation.surface: Reads like a dedication of Roman custom to the chief of the Greeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' here is clothing, as in a monk's habit, not a custom.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the loose outer garment worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Part of old town in area east of the Mediterranean

indicators.note: east of puts the words for in and area to the right of the sea, as on a map

parts.note: the Med is the usual short name for the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Describes the location of a district in some Levantine town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'area east of the Mediterranean' suggests the Middle East, but 'in' and 'area' simply follow MED.
explanation.definitionFit: A medina is the old walled quarter of a North African city, so it is part of an old town.

indicators.note: covering says the word for staff wraps round the numeral for one

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The physical education teachers supervise a single class.
explanation.definitionFit: A school period is one timetabled slot, the time given to a single lesson.

clue.text: South-eastern Tory fearing further parliamentary scrutiny

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory
dreading means fearing

explanation.surface: A Conservative MP from the south-east is anxious about a bill facing more debate.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament the second reading is the stage where a bill's main principles are debated.
explanation.definitionFit: The second reading is a later stage in which members examine a bill again, so it is more scrutiny.

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so the letter O
something not yet dead is still live, alive

explanation.surface: A duck of a greenish colour is still alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive names a dull yellowish-green colour like that of unripe olives.

clue.text: Theatre company has to stand for encore

parts.note: a rep is a repertory theatre company
to stand is to rise to one's feet

explanation.surface: The audience must get up for an actors' troupe's extra performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprise is a repeated performance of a piece, which is what an encore gives.

indicators.note: first off says the opening letter of the word for female servant is removed

parts.note: a maid is a female servant

explanation.surface: An instruction to assist a housemaid before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' reads as 'to begin with', but it drops the M of MAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid and help are synonyms as nouns or verbs, meaning assistance or to assist.

clue.text: Draw attention to offence involving cannabis

indicators.note: involving means the word for offence takes in the slang word for cannabis

parts.note: a slight is an insult that gives offence
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone wants to publicise a drug crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offence' looks like a crime but is an insult, SLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: To spotlight something is to focus public notice on it, an idiom from stage lighting.

clue.text: A large rodent mounting communion table

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means the word for rodent climbs upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A big rat climbs onto the church table.
explanation.definitionFit: The altar is the table in a church at which Holy Communion is celebrated.

parts.note: yew and ash are both trees

explanation.surface: Native woodland is decaying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rot' looks like decay, but here it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is slang for nonsense or humbug, and rot means the same talk.

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of wind that's are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone braces against a terrible gale.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand something is to hold out against it, a synonym for resist.

clue.text: Runner, perhaps, allowed to enter heat after training

indicators.note: to enter puts the word for allowed inside the other letters
after training says the letters of heat are reshaped into another order

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: A sprinter is permitted to run in a qualifying race once practice is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heat' looks like a qualifying race for the runner, but 'after training' rearranges its letters to ATHE, which 'to enter' then splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is one example of a sportsperson, so 'perhaps' marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Engineers showing signs of fatigue went to bed

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
showing signs of fatigue means tired

explanation.surface: Exhausted soldiers turned in for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire can mean to go to bed for the night, so the past tense fits 'went to bed'.

clue.text: Cotton material packed by Sassenach in Oban

indicators.note: packed by says the letters sit concealed within the run Sassenach in Oban

explanation.surface: An Englishman in a Scottish port carries cotton cloth in his luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: Sassenach is a Scots word for an English person; Oban is a Scottish west-coast town.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a twilled cotton fabric, used for trousers called chinos.

indicators.note: audibly says the word for developed is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: grown means developed or matured

explanation.surface: A shout of pain became clearly heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A groan is a low moan expressing pain or suffering.

indicators.note: regularly elusive means every other letter of proved slips away, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: An American author kept proving hard to pin down.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the first, third and fifth letters of 'proved' leaves the surname of Edgar Allan Poe.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was a nineteenth-century US author of tales and poems.
